mine: a notorious prisoner called Jesus Barabbas
note: SBLGNT (with Theta, family 1 and manuscripts known to Origen) reads "Iesoun Barabban" in 27:16-17, sharpening Pilate's choice between two men named Jesus; TR omits the first name, perhaps out of reverence. Context: Jesus Barabbas (SBLGNT) (medium confidence). SBLGNT reads Iesoun Barabban in 27:16-17 with Theta, family 1 and copies known to Origen, who disliked giving the name Jesus to a sinner; omission out of reverence is easier to explain than insertion, and Pilate's choice between two men called Jesus gains point. But the supporting witnesses are few, and NA28 brackets the name. Other possible meanings: (1) 'a notable prisoner, called Barabbas' — TR/Majority text, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus (whose 'ton Barabban' in 27:17 may preserve a trace of the name), most manuscripts, KJV, ESV, NASB, CSB. 'Jesus Barabbas' is read by NIV, NRSV and NET.
